title: Coarseness of coarse coding
summary: A one-dimensional square wave learned by linear gradient descent (9.3) on interval features, about 50 of them over the function's extent, with narrow, medium and broad intervals; training points uniform at random; α = 0.2/m (Figure 9.4). The draft only draws the widths and the wave; we use widths 0.08, 0.2 and 0.5 of the extent and a wave equal to 1 on its middle third.

facts.claim: Feature width strongly affects early learning (errors after 40 examples differ by more than 0.05) but hardly the final approximation (after 10,240 examples all within 0.01).

title: Mountain–car task
summary: The draft's dynamics and setup: v ← bound(v + 0.001A − 0.0025 cos 3p), p ← bound(p + v), with −1.2 ≤ p ≤ 0.5 and −0.07 ≤ v ≤ 0.07, velocity reset at the left bound, random starts; ten 9 × 9 tilings with random offsets; Sarsa(λ) of Figure 9.8 with replacing traces and clearing, λ = 0.9, ε = 0, α = 0.05. Optimistic zero initial values drive exploration. The policy at episode 100, frozen and run without learning, can still loop from some starts; learning on-line breaks such loops, so the claim concerns the learning episodes.

facts.claim: Linear Sarsa(λ) learns the task within 100 episodes: the first 10 episodes average over 400 steps, episodes 91–100 under 80.
Figure 9.11: replacing traces stay robust where accumulating traces blow up (λ = 0.9, α = 0.8/5), and λ = 1 is much worse than λ = 0.9 at α = 1.2/5.
Linear Watkins's Q(λ) (Figure 9.9) also learns the task.
